chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim and Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ibn Mukkan, all from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not buy the palm trees for one year until they bear fruit, even if they are bearing fruit, and if you wish to buy them for two years, then do so.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying palm trees before they bear fruit in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the conditions for valid sale of fruit-bearing trees (thamar), prohibiting the purchase of palms for a single year unless they have already produced fruit, thereby eliminating uncertainty (gharar) regarding the yield. The permissibility of a two-year period offers a practical alternative for buyers seeking to mitigate risk in agricultural transactions. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on clarity in contract terms to prevent dispute and exploitation in trade.
